title: Add profiles-as-code CLI + low-latency batch simulator (lb-sim) and loss-tolerant quant fallback planner
author: Anya Patel
description:
Motivation: enable reproducible, reviewable cost/profile changes (batching, cache, quantization) as code and provide a deterministic low-latency batch simulator (lb-sim) to validate SLO/cost tradeoffs before rollout. This PR introduces a lightweight CLI to manage profiles-as-code (YAML manifests), a simulation harness for microbatch and burst scenarios with latency distributions, and a loss-tolerant quantization fallback planner that provides safe fallbacks when aggressive quant profiles cause quality regressions.

What this PR contains: 
- profiles-as-code CLI (create/validate/preview/apply) and a profiles linter.
- lb-sim: a deterministic, seedable simulator that computes tail-latency and per-token cost given request mix, cache hit-rate, and batch policy.
- quant fallback planner: delta-based detector + rollback suggestion that ties to profiles-as-code outputs.
- example cost-profile templates and docs to onboard engineers and SREs.

Checklist: 
- [x] CLI commands + unit tests for YAML schema validation and lint rules
- [x] lb-sim core sim loop, scenario loader, and small e2e integration test (fast mode)
- [x] quant fallback planner algorithm + unit tests and integration with profiles preview
- [x] docs and example templates (docs/profiles-as-code.md, examples/cost-profile-template.yaml)
- [x] add telemetry hooks (metrics only) for sim runs and preview decisions

Testing: unit tests for CLI, simulation deterministic tests with fixed seeds, integration test that runs a representative 500-sample workload in 'fast' mode to verify no regressions in existing default profiles. Benchmarks: lb-sim run in CI quick mode completes in ~12s on CI runner.

Dependencies/compat: nothing external; pure Go + small Python helper for SDK integration tests. No breaking API changes; all changes gated behind CLI flags and feature flag redwood.profiles_as_code.

Related Linear/Jira: ENG-1182 (profiles as code RFC), PM-342 (cost optimization onboarding).
